---
title: "Bibliometric Analysis Learning Lab"
---

# Purpose

This project is a complete learning and teaching environment for reproducible bibliometric analysis in R. It moves from raw bibliographic exports to defensible interpretation and reporting.

The worked example uses a deterministic, synthetic ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) research corpus. It is designed to reproduce the metadata structure and analytical problems of a real drug-specific bibliometric study without distributing licensed Scopus or Web of Science records.

::: {.callout-note}
Every core analysis calls the original package function directly, such as
`bibliometrix::thematicMap()` or `bibliometrix::biblioNetwork()`. The project
does not hide analytical settings inside custom wrapper functions. Custom code
is restricted to generating and loading the synthetic teaching corpus.
:::

## What this course covers

1. Importing and auditing bibliographic records.
2. Deduplication and metadata cleaning.
3. Performance analysis.
4. Co-word thematic mapping.
5. Longitudinal thematic evolution.
6. Bibliographic coupling and co-citation.
7. Author, institution, and country collaboration.
8. Direct-citation historiography.
9. Linking themes to clinical populations, study designs, and funding.
10. Validation, reporting, and reproducibility.

## Learning outcomes

After completing the project, a learner should be able to:

- select an appropriate bibliographic database and export format;
- explain the difference between performance analysis and science mapping;
- distinguish co-word analysis, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, collaboration, and direct citation;
- construct and validate a thematic map;
- interpret centrality, density, theme evolution, splits, and merges;
- avoid treating automatic cluster labels as clinical conclusions;
- build a reproducible R and Quarto workflow; and
- teach the workflow using the included slides, exercises, and instructor guide.

## Recommended sequence

Complete Chapters 1–4 before attempting network analysis. Chapters 5–10 contain the main applied methods. Chapters 11–13 convert the analysis into a report, capstone assessment, and teaching programme.

::: {.callout-important}
Bibliometric software identifies statistical structures in metadata. Clinical meaning, eligibility, theme names, funding verification, and interpretation remain reviewer decisions.
:::

## Quick start

```bash
Rscript install_packages.R
quarto preview
```

To render the workshop slides:

```bash
quarto render slides/workshop.qmd
```

The analysis uses `bibliometrix` and follows the general workflow described by @aria2017 and the thematic-evolution framework of @cobo2011evolution.
